model_interpretation.claim: The measured 8x64 full-height tile was faster than baseline (3.061 μs versus 3.494 μs), while the 8x16 subtile was slower (3.839 μs); those timings do not establish a cause. Widening the full-height pencil to 16 may improve x coalescing and reduce the grid from 512 to 256 blocks versus 8x64, but doubles the block to 1024 threads and may reduce occupancy. This isolates the wider full-slab tradeoff while retaining the existing halo logic for correctness.

model_interpretation.claim: A 16x32 x/y-subtile keeps blocks at 512 threads like the selected 8x64 full-height parent, while doubling x width and splitting y into two tiles. Compared with prior subtiles, it reduces relative halo duplication versus 16x16 (25% versus 50% of core elements) and uses one barrier, but introduces halo global loads and may trade occupancy against coalescing. The 16x64 and 8x64/8x16 measurements show different latencies but do not establish which factor caused them; this candidate tests the distinct 16x32 geometry without presuming a win.

model_interpretation.claim: The selected 8x64 parent measured 3.061 μs versus the 3.494 μs baseline, but that result does not establish whether a full-height tile is preferable. Holding the x pencil at 8 while producing 16 y rows per block may reduce threads per block from 512 to 128 and increase block-level parallelism, at the cost of loading four halo rows on each of four subtiles and thus duplicating halo traffic. Directly loading halo values with the established period-63 mapping also reduces the tile synchronization to one barrier. The competing occupancy, halo-traffic, and synchronization effects require measurement; no winner is presumed.
